summary: Reproduced and corrected the two concrete failed-session recovery defects identified while reviewing candidate PR 1101: probing was disabled by default, and a stale successful probe could erase a newer transfer failure. The candidate's valid recovery coverage was preserved. The underlying cause of the reported recurring distributed transfer failures remains unverified.

tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before reproduction: the unset probe flag evaluated false and an in-flight successful probe erased a concurrently recorded newer failure; 2 failed, 9 passed, and 3 subtests passed.

Passing-after regression and boundary coverage: 12 passed and 3 subtests passed, including default enablement, explicit opt-out, stale-probe isolation, failed probes, probe exceptions, and native wrapper delegation.
Changed Python production and test files compiled successfully.
The patch contains no whitespace errors.
Candidate PR 1101 changed no production Python source relative to the recorded base.

gpu_execution.evidence: Environment inspection found one AMD Instinct MI355X gfx950 GPU, not the reported NVIDIA/XCCL multi-node RoCEv2 deployment. No GPU execution was used as substitute evidence for the control-plane regression or unavailable distributed workload.

remaining_limitations: The original 5-prefill/3-decode GLM5.2 workload and model weights were unavailable.
The reported NVIDIA CUDA/XCCL multi-node RoCEv2 topology was unavailable; the host exposed one AMD gfx950 GPU with ROCm 7.2.
The issue provides no minimal reproducer for the recurring transfer failures, so their underlying cause was not identified or corrected.
No native source changed. The installed Mooncake extension was inspected and exposes TransferEngine.send_probe, but no native library was rebuilt.
